candidates.name: Illumina Windows 10 support timeline for instrument PCs: older NovaSeq 6000 units run LTSB 1607, whose extended support ends 13 Oct 2026; newer units run LTSC 1809, supported to 9 Jan 2029
candidates.access: Opened with WebFetch, no login. Knowledge Article #9668 lists the NovaSeq 6000 on 'Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB (build 1607)… extended support through October 13, 2026' or LTSC 1809 'through January 09, 2029'. It also says Illumina 'does not support upgrading… to Windows 11' and will give more information about OS upgrades 'prior to any OS End of Life'. Companion page (opened): https://knowledge.illumina.com/instrumentation/general/instrumentation-general-faq-list/000006353 maps model 30.0.C06.* to LTSB 1607 and model 30.1.C01.* to LTSC 1809 ('depends on manufacturing date and the current software image'). Older upgrade FAQ (search snippet only): https://knowledge.illumina.com/instrumentation/general/instrumentation-general-faq-list/000002247 says upgrades need a Field Service Engineer visit, are covered under an active service contract and are quoted otherwise. Next steps for the test agent: (1) re-fetch the 2 KB pages after 13 Oct 2026 to see whether the 1607 line changed; (2) search support.illumina.com/bulletins and knowledge.illumina.com for 'NovaSeq 6000' with '1809', 'LTSC', 'OS upgrade' or 'end of support' from 2026; (3) search hospital and university IT-security policy pages for 'NovaSeq' with 'unsupported operating system', 'network isolation' or 'Windows 10 exception'; (4) check the latest NovaSeq Control Software release notes (assets.illumina.com …/software/novaseq/) for a new OS image.
candidates.rationale: This is a new forensic clock for the 6000 tail. An early-build 6000 (model 30.0.C06, i.e. the first manufacturing years, 2017 to about 2019) loses Windows extended security support tomorrow. Clinical labs under HIPAA and CAP IT rules then have three choices: pay for a field-service OS re-image, isolate the box from the network, or retire it. The second date, LTSC 1809 ending 9 Jan 2029, is a practical hard ceiling on the 6000's life, because Illumina says it will not move instruments to Windows 11. That date fits our extrapolated tail end of about 2029 to 2031 and argues against management's claim that the tail is 'permanent'. Read it both ways. If Illumina quietly offers free 1809 re-images, the oldest units get about 2 more years, which supports a sticky tail in 2027. If it charges for re-images or gives no path, 2027 conversion becomes more likely, which supports about 5 more points of mix shift. Also worth recording: what share of the roughly 1,360-unit base is the 30.0.C06 model (from serial ranges or forum posts).

candidates.name: Japan PMDA package inserts (添付文書) and MHLW insurance-coverage documents for NGS cancer genomic-profiling tests: which sequencer each approved test names, and any partial-change approvals (一部変更承認) adding the NovaSeq X
candidates.access: Seen only as search-result snippets, not opened. Related hits: https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/10901000/000486801.pdf (Todai OncoPanel workflow) and https://www.icrweb.jp/mod/resource/view.php?id=468 (lecture listing sequencers registered as medical devices in Japan). Method: use PMDA's public IVD and device package-insert search (pmda.go.jp/PmdaSearch, no login) with product names FoundationOne CDx, FoundationOne Liquid CDx, GenMineTOP, Todai OncoPanel, Guardant360 CDx, TruSight Oncology Comprehensive and OncoGuide NCC. Read the 使用機器 / 組み合わせて使用する医療機器 field and the revision dates (改訂). Then search Japanese for 'NovaSeq X 届出 医療機器' and 'NovaSeq 6000Dx 製造販売届出' to see whether Illumina has registered any X as a Japanese medical device.
candidates.rationale: Japan reimburses comprehensive genomic profiling nationally, and every approved test is locked to a registered sequencer. Approvals are dated, so version-by-version package inserts give a second regulated-tail clock outside the US. If no Japanese approved test names the X 3 years after launch, that supports a long regulated tail with no conversion (high-price 6000 revenue persists, which cuts against the 2027 conversion piece of 1A). If insert revisions in 2025–26 add the X, that measures how long conversion takes for regulated tests and suggests 2027 conversion. This angle is distinct from the US openFDA PMA work already done.

candidates.name: Palmetto MolDX Technical Assessment FAQ and TA forms: does changing the sequencer from the 6000 to the X trigger a new TA or Z-code revalidation for Medicare-billed LDTs?
candidates.access: Seen only as a search-result snippet; not opened. The snippet says a test validated within a larger panel or platform validation is acceptable; FAQ dated Jul 2023. Forms PDF (snippet): https://dominoapps.palmettogba.com/palmetto/providers.nsf/Files/MolDX_Technical_Assessment_Forms.pdf/$FILE/MolDX_Technical_Assessment_Forms.pdf (Apr 2025 checklist GEN-CQM-003). Fetch both and search for 'platform', 'instrument', 'modification', 'change' and 'resubmit'. Then search palmettogba.com and the DEX site for 'test modification' or 'significant change' guidance from 2025–26.
candidates.rationale: This would quantify the switching cost that keeps clinical labs on the 6000. If MolDX requires a full TA resubmission (months of review, risk to Medicare payment) for a platform change, that explains a volume-inelastic clinical tail. Labs on Medicare-billed MRD and CGP LDTs would then delay conversion until a new assay version ships, which fits Thaysen's 'cohort 2'. If a platform change only needs a notification, the regulatory moat is weaker and 2027 conversion is more likely. This is an untried, primary-document angle on why the remaining 6000 users stay.

candidates.name: Illumina NovaSeq 6000 service-plan SKUs and prices on the GSA distributor page (Gold Support Plan 20020137), compared with NovaSeq X service plans
candidates.access: Seen only as a search-result snippet ('NovaSeq 6000 Warranty Upgrade: Gold Support Plan'); not opened. Fetch the page and record the price and any date. Then fetch sibling SKUs for the 6000 Silver/Bronze plans and the NovaSeq X plans (search govsci.com for 'NovaSeq X Support Plan'). Compare the 6000 service price with the X service price, and with 2024–25 snippets if any exist.
candidates.rationale: The GSA catalog was used before for reagent SKUs, not for service contracts. Rising 6000 service-contract prices (or plans withdrawn from the catalog) would be a quiet lever Illumina uses to push the tail onto the X: the 6000 costs more to keep running, which hints at an end-of-life schedule. Flat or cheap 6000 service would support management's 'stays for years' view. Payoff is lower because S565 found the distributor catalog patchy.

apify_requests.why: Public LinkedIn posts by clinical lab staff announcing a 6000 retirement or a clinical go-live on the X are a dated, lab-by-lab census of conversion in 2025–26, with lab names and timing. The job-postings work does not cover this. The results would show whether clinical conversions are still flowing (a supporting signal for about 5 points in 2027) or have dried up (a frozen tail).
